old_caption: The video captures a serene natural scene featuring a calm river flowing through a lush forest. The river's surface is smooth, reflecting the surrounding greenery and the sky above. The trees on either side of the river are dense and vibrant, with leaves in various shades of green, suggesting it might be late spring or summer. The sunlight filters through the foliage, creating dappled patterns on the water's surface and highlighting the tranquility of the setting. There are no visible animals or people in the scene, emphasizing the untouched beauty of nature. The camera remains stationary throughout the video, allowing viewers to fully absorb the peaceful ambiance of the forested riverbank.

caption: The video captures a slow-moving stream winding through dense summer woodland, filmed from a fixed viewpoint at water level. Lush green trees line both banks beneath a pale sky, mirrored in the foreground water alongside a bright sky patch. A grey rock protrudes left of center, a fallen log rests along the right bank, and leafy branches hang in the near right foreground. Across the clip, the water surface keeps shimmering with low-amplitude ripples, making the tree and sky reflections wobble and distort subtly. Small bright specks remain scattered on the surface, while a slightly faster rippling stretch persists in the middle distance where the channel narrows. The banks, rock, and log hold their positions throughout, with nothing entering or leaving.

This is a TEMPORALLY CROPPED EXCERPT from a longer video, not a complete event or a loop.

endpoints are normal, not physical errors. Do not add unseen causes, onset, stopping or outcomes.
An internal editing cut is not evidence of physical motion connecting the views.

Check identification before physical interpretation: a reflection is not a separate actor;
a powder/smoke/liquid outline or shadow is not automatically the boundary of a solid object;
an apparent change caused by occlusion/viewpoint is not automatically material deformation.
Do not claim contact, bending, compression, melting, disintegration or structural recovery unless
the appropriate material/surface itself provides visible evidence. Do not infer a force or earlier
collision just because the visible configuration would be compatible with it.
Compare several frames before asserting translation, rotation, direction, unchanged position or
camera tracking. A single visible texture/seam does not prove spin. Avoid unnecessary absolute
claims of stillness, no motion, no camera motion or 'exactly' synchronized changes.
Remove invented scene details and explanations, but keep clearly visible ongoing motion and
processes. Avoid deleting the real process merely because its cause lies outside the cropped window.

This is a direct video description, not an analysis note. No mandatory beginning/end formula.
Complete every sentence. If accuracy requires a substantial length difference, explain it outside
